preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

# NotByDefault

**Prove the choice. Recheck the decision.**

AI coding agents pick models, databases and SDKs by default and give a reason. NotByDefault checks whether that reason is true on your project's own data, records the evidence, and reopens the decision when a requirement, price or fact changes.

> No decision without a why.

## Example

An agent picked `openai/gpt-oss-120b` for an action-items endpoint because it was "cost-effective, strong at extraction, widely used". On the project's 12 cases it scored 10/12 at $418/mo, over the $375 budget. The cheapest setup that meets the bar is 10/12 at gpt-oss-20b + verifier, $336/mo: **$418→$336/mo, $81.56/mo saved**. `notbydefault resolve 21` recommends that switch and stops there: adding a verifier loop to the code isn't automated yet, so it changes nothing.

Full comparison between candidates: gpt-oss-20b + verifier is the cheapest in-budget recommendation at $336/mo; gemini-3.1-flash-lite scored higher (11/12 vs 10/12) but $345/mo is still under budget — the ranking depends on whether you prioritize cost or correctness. See the fit-check table.

When the requirement "data must stay in the EU" was added, #21 flipped to **stale** (Groq documents US-only; the chosen stack can't meet the new requirement), and so did an older Groq decision. MongoDB went to **needs_review**: where its data lives depends on how it's deployed. Stale means a known fact breaks it; needs_review means a human should judge.

Live trace in neatlogs: `0f65667e9f5c521dfc124c89f188f9ca` (71 real provider requests across a quota reset, $0.0461 ($0.0461 across two attempts; stop-and-resume saves cached work) at list price on free tiers).

## How it works

1. **Catch.** A Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook spots a decision when the agent writes a model name, installs an SDK or edits a manifest. It targets under 300 ms (p50 under 200 ms; worst case 405 ms under full-suite load) and never blocks the agent.
2. **Record.** The decision, the agent's stated reason and the code it touches go into a decision graph (SQLite, stored with the repo).
3. **Check the reasons.** `claims` splits the reason into cost, quality, latency, compliance and popularity claims, and gives each a verdict with a source. "Widely used" is never evidence for your project.
4. **Check the choice.** `check` runs several candidates on your own cases. Verifiers catch bad outputs, two judges from different model families score them, and confidence intervals flag runs that are too close to call.
5. **Act.** `resolve` applies the winner on a branch (`nbd/<id>-<slug>`), edits only that decision's call sites, generates tests from past failures and writes the PR text. It never touches main or pushes.
6. **Watch.** Each decision stores its assumptions: budget, volume, prices, data region, requirements. `watch` and `require` reopen the affected decisions when any of them change.
7. **Review.** `ui` shows the decision graph, a receipt per decision with its full evidence, a change timeline, eval results and costs. `scan` scores the repo's decision debt (the demo repo scores 14).

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `notbydefault check <id>` | Fit-check a decision on your own cases |
| `notbydefault claims <id>` | Verdict on each claim in the agent's reason |
| `notbydefault resolve <id>` | Apply the winner on a branch, with tests and PR text |
| `notbydefault require <project> "<text>"` | Add a requirement; mark decisions stale or needs_review |
| `notbydefault watch` | Reopen decisions whose assumptions changed |
| `notbydefault why "<question>"` | Answer from recorded decisions only, with sources |
| `notbydefault scan` | Decision debt: unchecked choices, false claims, expired assumptions |
| `notbydefault ui` | Web UI with the live decision graph |

## Quickstart

```bash
pip install -e .
cp .env.example .env         # add GROQ_API_KEY and GEMINI_API_KEY
notbydefault init demo-app
notbydefault check 21 --project demo-app
notbydefault ui --project demo-app
```

To rebuild the full demo scenario on a throwaway copy:

```bash
python scripts/demo_dataset.py --out .demo-dataset/demo-app --offline
```

## Results

On our own evals, decision detection improved from 0.81 to 1.00 recall over three versions. Pivot recall 0.67 → 1.00 on original cases; 0.5 on held-out cases (v2 and v3). We ship with the lower number visible — held-out is where the next version has to improve. 475 tests, no network.

## Sponsor tools

- **neatlogs:** every model call, verifier and hook traced as spans with tokens and cost.
  - Model calls go to Groq and Google AI Studio over HTTPS. Your project data (notes, cases, code paths) is sent to those providers as prompts. No calls to Anthropic or OpenAI. When `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` is set, prompts and outputs are also sent to neatlogs. When it's not set, no spans leave the machine.
- **Entire:** Entire's Graph finds the callers affected by each decision (so `resolve #21` edits `actions.py` but leaves `app.py` alone — decision #13's own evidence rejected Gemini for summaries). Checkpoints link decisions to the agent session that made them.
- **cfo.ai:** Pricing modeled with Ari (cfo.ai): $49/team/month Starter, $149/month Growth. Revised base case is self-funded through October 2027 under disclosed assumptions. Full plan: `business/plan.md`.

## Business case

NotByDefault reviews AI coding agents' technical choices against the project's own data and checks their stated reasoning, with proposed launch pricing of $49 per team per month. In our demo, one model-selection decision reduced projected inference costs by $82/month at the same accuracy on the project's own cases (10/12) — enough to cover the subscription if those savings persist. Our revised 12-month plan starts with $5,000 of founder cash, two pre-launch pilot customers at $49, 20% upgrade to $149 Growth in the third paid month, and a staged founder draw ($0 Nov–Apr, $2k/mo May–Oct) — resulting in a self-funded year with ~$5,354 ending cash and $2,789 MRR by October 2027 under disclosed assumptions.

## Known limitations

- Live demo may require a resume across days when provider free-tier quotas reset; the check saves state and resumes without duplicating requests.
- Eval results are measured on our own cases with held-out cases written before fixes. Not independently labeled.
- `test_hook_is_fast` is a timing flake (300 ms limit); passes when run alone.

| `notbydefault why "<question>"` | Answer from recorded decisions only, with sources |
| `notbydefault scan` | Decision debt: unchecked choices, false claims, expired assumptions |
| `notbydefault ui` | Web UI with the live decision graph |

## Quickstart

```bash
pip install -e .
cp .env.example .env         # add GROQ_API_KEY and GEMINI_API_KEY
notbydefault init demo-app
notbydefault check 21 --project demo-app
notbydefault ui --project demo-app
```

To rebuild the full demo scenario on a throwaway copy:

```bash
python scripts/demo_dataset.py --out .demo-dataset/demo-app --offline
```

## Results

On our own evals, decision detection improved from 0.81 to 1.00 recall over three versions. Pivot recall 0.67 → 1.00 on original cases; 0.5 on held-out cases (v2 and v3). We ship with the lower number visible — held-out is where the next version has to improve. 475 tests, no network.

## Sponsor tools

- **neatlogs:** every model call, verifier and hook traced as spans with tokens and cost.
  - Model calls go to Groq and Google AI Studio over HTTPS. Your project data (notes, cases, code paths) is sent to those providers as prompts. No calls to Anthropic or OpenAI. When `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` is set, prompts and outputs are also sent to neatlogs. When it's not set, no spans leave the machine.
- **Entire:** Entire's Graph finds the callers affected by each decision (so `resolve #21` edits `actions.py` but leaves `app.py` alone — decision #13's own evidence rejected Gemini for summaries). Checkpoints link decisions to the agent session that made them.
- **cfo.ai:** Pricing modeled with Ari (cfo.ai): $49/team/month Starter, $149/month Growth. Revised base case is self-funded through October 2027 under disclosed assumptions. Full plan: `business/plan.md`.

## Business case

NotByDefault reviews AI coding agents' technical choices against the project's own data and checks their stated reasoning, with proposed launch pricing of $49 per team per month. In our demo, one model-selection decision reduced projected inference costs by $82/month at the same accuracy on the project's own cases (10/12) — enough to cover the subscription if those savings persist. Our revised 12-month plan starts with $5,000 of founder cash, two pre-launch pilot customers at $49, 20% upgrade to $149 Growth in the third paid month, and a staged founder draw ($0 Nov–Apr, $2k/mo May–Oct) — resulting in a self-funded year with ~$5,354 ending cash and $2,789 MRR by October 2027 under disclosed assumptions.

## Known limitations

- Live demo may require a resume across days when provider free-tier quotas reset; the check saves state and resumes without duplicating requests.
- Eval results are measured on our own cases with held-out cases written before fixes. Not independently labeled.
- `test_hook_is_fast` is a timing flake (300 ms limit); passes when run alone.

content.content:
"""Build a demo dataset that exercises every part of NotByDefault, on a throwaway copy of demo-app.

    python scripts/demo_dataset.py --out .demo-dataset/demo-app [--offline] [--no-shots]

--out is reset from demo-app/ (graph.db copied via SQLite's backup API, so the live graph is never
touched), made a git repo on main, and then:
  0. watch      record each decision's assumptions (baseline)
  1. reasons    a SCRIPTED agent reason on #13, #21, MongoDB, OpenAI and gpt-4o (stored as
                agent_reason, its source saying so: demo-app's own sessions recorded none)
  2. resolve 21 dry run, then --apply on branch nbd/21-... (commit answered "yes", on the copy).
                When the verdict recommends a "+ verifier" setup, resolve stops at its
                recommendation (adding a verifier loop to the code is not automated yet) and both
                runs record that; #21 then stays on its current model
  3. pivot      the user types PIVOT_PROMPT. The real Pivot Check runs first; when it records
                nothing (its prefilter or confirm call says no, or --offline has no cached
                answer), ONE pivot is written from SEEDED_PIVOT, marked source=seeded
     + an agent turn: the PreToolUse hook catches a new model choice, its reason read from a
                scripted transcript (scripts/demo_transcript.jsonl)
  4. claims     on #21 first, then the other reasoned decisions and the agent turn's
  5. require    REQUIREMENT: Groq documents US only -> every decision still on Groq goes stale
                (#13, and #21 unless resolve moved it); a decision whose region depends on the
                deployment (MongoDB) -> needs review
  6. watch      re-evaluate the assumptions ('data region: any' broken on #21)
  7. scan       decision debt
  8. shots      regenerate docs/screenshots (light + dark) from the dataset; --no-shots skips it

Every step prints the trace id it created, the graph ids it added or changed and the files it
wrote. Model calls are answered from the copy's response cache (carried over from the previous
build unless --fresh); every call that would go to a provider is printed with its step. With

# Demo claims audit

Audited 2026-10-12 against the files in this repo (commit `e908b29` plus the untracked
`demo-live-run.txt`). Nothing in application logic, evaluation outputs or results files was changed.

## Status labels

- **Verified**: recomputed in this audit from a raw results file, cache or eval output, and it matches.
- **Projected**: the arithmetic checks out, but the figure is a forecast built on stated assumptions,
  not a measurement (every $/month figure falls in this category).
- **Reported, unverified**: written somewhere in the repo, but this audit could not check it against raw data.
- **Seeded / scripted**: written by `scripts/demo_dataset.py` for the demo, and labeled as such in the data.
- **Superseded**: true for an earlier run, but no longer what the code or data produce.

## The runs

There are two real fit checks of decision #21. They are **not interchangeable**: the verdict changed between them.

| | Run A (earlier) | Run B (latest) |
|---|---|---|
| Trace | `4bcff389ab979638e4ffa7ee88619318` | `0f65667e9f5c521dfc124c89f188f9ca` (final); `56a5915f9768ef65b7f21546bdfceb6a` (partial, first attempt) |
| Results file | `demo-app/.notbydefault/results/21-20261011T070521Z.json` | `demo-app/.notbydefault/results/21-20261012T070725Z.json` |
| Run at | 2026-10-11 07:05 UTC | 2026-10-12 07:07 UTC (attempt 1 at 2026-10-11 20:30 UTC hit a Gemini daily limit; resumed after the reset) |
| Requests | 31 made, 42 from an existing cache (**not** a fresh live run) | 71 live requests into a fresh cache `cache-live-20261011T202940Z` (56 + 15), 5 models |
| Today's setup (gpt-oss-120b) | 10/12, 6/8 hard, **$407.35/mo** | 10/12, 6/8 hard, **$418.04/mo** |
| gpt-oss-20b + verifier | 10/12, 6/8 hard, $385.37/mo, **over budget** | 10/12, 6/8 hard, $336.48/mo, **in budget** |
| gemini-3.1-flash-lite | 11/12, 8/8 hard, $345.07/mo, in budget | 11/12, 8/8 hard, $345.07/mo, in budget |
| Verdict | switch to **gemini-3.1-flash-lite** (saves $62.28/mo) | switch to **gpt-oss-20b + verifier** (saves $81.56/mo); best quality in budget: flash-lite |
| What `resolve 21` does | applied flash-lite on a branch (demo dataset build, see C10) | recommends the switch and **stops**: a verifier loop can't be added to the code automatically yet |
| Documented in | commits `44b4fc1`, `3956607`; `eval/results/v3.json`; README before `60a13ca` | README, ARCHITECTURE.md, decision record `0002`, `business/costs.*`, `docs/demo.md`, `demo-live-run.txt` |

Both runs used the same 12 cases (8 hard), verifier `21.py` (sha `62bd632d5177ad7f`), volume assumptions
(20,000 users x 60 calls) and $375 budget. I recomputed every row in the table above from each results
file's raw `rows` (cost per call x 1,200,000 calls), and they match the reports to the cent.

**Why the verdict flipped:** list prices didn't change. Run to run, gpt-oss-20b + verifier's measured
cost per call fell from $0.000321 to $0.000280 (fewer retries), which moved it from $10.37 over budget
to $38.52 under. gpt-oss-120b's cost rose from $0.000340 to $0.000348. So **the recommended setup is
sensitive to sampling variance in retries and output length.** flash-lite's numbers were identical in
both runs: 11/12, $345.07, in budget.

## Claims

| # | Claim | Source | Run / trace | Status | Recommended wording |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Today's gpt-oss-120b: 10/12 correct (6/8 hard) | results B `rows`; decision record 0002; README | B `0f65667e` | **Verified** (also 10/12 in run A) | "Today's model got 10 of 12 of the project's own test cases right." |
| C2 | Today's setup costs $418/month | results B; costs.csv | B | **Projected.** The arithmetic is verified: $0.0003484/call x 20,000 users x 60 calls. 20,000 users and the $375 budget are "demo scenario assumption"s in the graph, and 60 calls/user is marked ASSUMPTION. List prices were fetched 2026-10-10 and the run used free tiers. | "At an assumed 1.2M calls a month, about $418/month: over the $375 budget." |
| C3 | gpt-oss-20b + verifier: 10/12, $336/month, in budget | results B | B | **Verified** score; **projected** cost. Hard cases 6/8, same as today's. Item F1 is 0.88 vs 0.94 and judge scores are 4.25–4.33 vs 4.83, so it matches on *case correctness* but scores lower on the secondary quality measures. It was **over budget in run A** ($385.37). | "The cheapest setup that clears the bar also got 10 of 12, at a projected $336/month." |
| C4 | Net saving $81.56/month ($418.04 → $336.48) | results B; decision record; costs.csv; README | B | **Projected.** The arithmetic is verified: 418.04 − 336.48 = 81.56. It isn't realized, because `resolve` doesn't apply this setup (C11), and it isn't stable across runs (run A: this setup was over budget). | "A projected ~$82/month saving at the assumed volume, if the switch is made." Don't say "saved". |

No branch or record of it exists in the current `.demo-dataset` (only `main`, one baseline commit). | **Don't use.** If you show resolve, show what it does now: it recommends and stops. |
| C11 | "`resolve 21` recommends that switch and stops" | README; demo_dataset.py docstring | B | **Verified** in code docs and the current demo dataset (#21 is still on gpt-oss-120b) | Keep as is. |

| C14 | Seeded pivot "drop the verifiers" | demo dataset node 32 `source: seeded` | demo dataset | **Seeded**, labeled in the data | If shown, say it's a seeded example. |

- The `demo-live-run.txt` header says "inputs: 12 (8 from failure bank …)", but the report body and results B say 7 cases were re-run from the failure bank (run A: 6).

**Reproducibility limit:** I didn't re-run `check 21` against the cache, because that would write

5. "Best quality within budget: `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`. 11 of 12, all 8 hard cases, projected $345 a month, but much slower (about 14 s vs 1.5 s)."

I've written the audit to `docs/demo_claims_audit.md`. It contains a 20-row claims table plus a recommended script for the video. I didn't touch any code, results files or other docs, and I haven't committed anything.

## What I found

**There are two real runs of the #21 check, and they disagree on the recommendation.**

| | Run A, trace `4bcff389` (Oct 11) | Run B, trace `0f65667e` (Oct 12) |
|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-120b today | 10/12, $407/mo | 10/12, $418/mo |
| gpt-oss-20b + verifier | 10/12, $385/mo, **over budget** | 10/12, $336/mo, **in budget** |
| gemini-3.1-flash-lite | 11/12, 8/8 hard, $345/mo | identical |
| Recommendation | switch to flash-lite | switch to gpt-oss-20b + verifier |

- **The numbers check out.** I recomputed every figure above from the raw rows in each run's results file, and they match the reports to the cent.
- **The recommendation flipped because of run-to-run noise, not a price change.** The cheaper setup needed fewer verifier retries in run B, which moved it from $10 over the $375 budget to $39 under. That makes the $81.56 figure a projection, and not a stable one.
- **All $/month figures are projections.** They assume 20,000 users × 60 calls a month at list price, and the checks ran on free tiers. The saving also hasn't happened: `resolve` can't apply a verifier setup yet, so it stops at the recommendation.
- **Don't use 0/12 → 12/12.** It came from the demo dataset applying flash-lite under run A's recommendation. Under run B, `resolve` changes no code and generates no tests, and no branch or record of that result exists any more.
- **The agent's quoted reason is scripted.** "Cost-effective, strong at extraction, widely used" comes from `scripts/demo_dataset.py`, labelled there as not from a real session, but the README presents it as a real agent's reasoning. The "drop the verifiers" pivot is also seeded.
- **Smaller issues:**
  - The same run has three different "check cost" figures. Only $0.0461 covers both attempts.
  - The run header in `demo-live-run.txt` says 8 failure-bank cases, but there were 7.
  - "Same accuracy" is true only for cases correct. The cheaper setup scores lower on item F1 (0.88 vs 0.94) and on the judges' scores.
- **Also confirmed:** the 71 live requests to 5 models, the eval recall figures, and the 475-test count (I collected the tests but didn't run them).
- **Not checked:** the hook latency, the decision-debt score of 14, the business projections, and whether the trace actually opens in neatlogs.

## Strongest defensible story

Use run B only: it's the only fully live run, and every number traces back to its results file. One limit: I didn't replay it from the cache, because that would write new results and graph entries.

## Claims to use in the video

1. "Say an agent picks gpt-oss-120b because it's 'cost-effective, strong at extraction, widely used'." (Caption it as an example reason.)
2. "NotByDefault tests that choice on the project's own 12 cases, 8 of them hard: three models, each alone and with a verifier, scored against reference answers by two blind judges."

4. "Cheapest setup that clears the bar: gpt-oss-20b plus a verifier. Also 10 of 12, at a projected $336 a month, about $82 a month less."
5. "Best quality within budget: gemini-3.1-flash-lite, 11 of 12 with all 8 hard cases, at $345 a month, but about 9× slower."
6. "71 real requests to 5 models, resumed across a free-tier quota reset, under 5 cents at list price."
7. "`resolve` recommends the switch and stops: adding a verifier loop to the code isn't automated yet."
8. (Optional) "Add 'data must stay in the EU', and the Groq decisions go stale while MongoDB is flagged for review."

Caption: *"Costs are list-price projections at an assumed 20,000 users × 60 calls/month. 12 cases: one case = 8 points."*

**Avoid:** $407, $62 saved, 0/12 → 12/12, "resolve switched it", "saved $81.56", "same quality", and $0.0221 or $0.0561 as the run's cost.

Prepare NotByDefault for a clean, reproducible hackathon demonstration. Work in the existing repository.

## Goal
I need to record real terminal, dashboard, and GitHub footage for a short promotional video. Do not generate fake UI or fake terminal output.

## Tasks
1. Inspect the current README, CLI help, demo scripts, docs/demo.md, dashboard routes, and the demo claims audit if it exists.
2. Identify the shortest reliable sequence demonstrating:
   - A captured technical decision and its stated reason.
   - Claim verification.
   - Workload-specific comparison of alternatives.
   - A decision receipt containing evidence.
   - A changed requirement causing the appropriate `stale` or `needs_review` state.
3. Verify the exact commands against the current CLI implementation. Do not guess command syntax.
4. Determine which parts require real API calls and which can be reproduced offline. Respect existing cost caps and caches; never bypass quota protections.
5. Create `docs/recording_plan.md` containing:
   - Exact commands in execution order.
   - Expected results, grounded in actual code or verified outputs.
   - What I should show on screen for each step.
   - Approximate clip duration.
   - Whether each clip is essential or optional.
   - Setup and cleanup instructions.
6. Include a recovery plan for rate limits, cached results, and dashboard startup failures.
7. Check whether the actual resolve flow and GitHub PR exist and are safe to demonstrate. If not, flag this instead of fabricating a PR.

## Safety
- Do not expose API keys, `.env` values, private data, or sensitive environment output.
- Do not run expensive live evaluations without checking their configured cost cap.
- Do not push, commit, or modify production branches.
- Prefer a disposable copy or existing demo dataset where appropriate.
- Do not claim that seeded offline data is a live detection.

Do not add features. Prepare the smallest convincing demonstration of the existing product and report any blockers that require my manual action.

def note_traces(step: str, text: str) -> None:
    for t in dict.fromkeys(TRACE.findall(text)):
        if (step, t) not in traces:
            traces.append((step, t))
            print(f"[trace] {step}: {t}")


# --- what each step changed ----------------------------------------------------------------

def graph_state(p: Path) -> dict[int, tuple[str, str, str]]:
    from notbydefault.graph import Graph
    with Graph.for_project(p) as g:
        return {n["id"]: (n["type"], n["label"], hashlib.sha1(json.dumps(
            n["data"], sort_keys=True, default=str).encode()).hexdigest()) for n in g.nodes()}


def file_state(*roots: Path) -> dict[str, tuple[int, int]]:
    out = {}
    for root in roots:
        for f in root.rglob("*"):
            rel = f.relative_to(root).parts
            if not f.is_file() or ".git" in rel or "__pycache__" in rel or "cache" in rel:
                continue
            st = f.stat()
            out[str(f)] = (st.st_mtime_ns, st.st_size)
    return out


class Step:
    """Prints the graph ids a step added or changed and the files it wrote."""

    def __init__(self, p: Path, name: str):
        self.p, self.name = p, name

    def __enter__(self):
        say(self.name)
        self.g, self.f = graph_state(self.p), file_state(self.p, SHOTS)
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        if exc[0]:
            return False
        g, f = graph_state(self.p), file_state(self.p, SHOTS)
        for nid, (kind, label, h) in g.items():
            if nid not in self.g:
                print(f"[graph] +#{nid} {kind} {label!r}")
            elif self.g[nid][2] != h:
                print(f"[graph] ~#{nid} {kind} {label!r}")
        for path in sorted(set(f) - set(self.f)) + sorted(
                x for x in f if x in self.f and f[x] != self.f[x]):
            rel = os.path.relpath(path, REPO)
            print(f"[file]  {rel}")
            written.append(rel)
        return False


def captured(step: str, fn, *a, **kw):
    """Run fn with out=list.append, print its lines, collect the trace ids it reports."""
    lines: list[str] = []
    code = fn(*a, out=lines.append, **kw)
    text = "\n".join(lines)
    print(text)
    note_traces(step, text)
    return code, text


def git(p: Path, *args: str) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=p, capture_output=True, text=True,
                          check=True).stdout.strip()


# --- model calls ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def providers(p: Path, offline: bool):
    """The project's ProviderSet, answering from the response cache; every call that would reach
    a provider is printed with its step, and refused when offline."""
    from notbydefault.fit.providers import ProviderSet, load_catalog
    from notbydefault.llm import OfflineCacheMiss

    class Logged(ProviderSet):
        step = ""

        def _transport(self, provider: str):        # only reached on a cache miss
            if offline:
                print(f"[live call skipped: --offline] step {self.step!r} -> {provider}")
                raise OfflineCacheMiss(f"--offline: no cached answer, live {provider} call skipped")
            print(f"[live call] step {self.step!r} -> {provider}")
            return super()._transport(provider)

    return Logged(load_catalog(p), cache_dir=p / ".notbydefault" / "cache",
                  env={} if offline else None)


# --- steps ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _remove(path: Path) -> None:
    """rmtree that also removes git's read-only object files (Windows)."""
    import stat

    def writable(func, p, _exc):
        os.chmod(p, stat.S_IWRITE)
        func(p)
    shutil.rmtree(path, onexc=writable)


def copy_demo(dest: Path, fresh: bool = False) -> Path:
    """Fresh copy; the previous build's model-response cache is carried over (unless `fresh`),
    so a rebuild answers the same prompts from it instead of calling a provider again."""
    src = REPO / "demo-app"
    if dest.resolve() == src.resolve():
        raise SystemExit("--out must not be demo-app itself")
    keep = None
    if dest.exists():
        old_cache = dest / ".notbydefault" / "cache"
        if old_cache.is_dir() and not fresh:
            keep = dest.parent / ".cache-carry"
            shutil.rmtree(keep, ignore_errors=True)
            shutil.copytree(old_cache, keep)
        _remove(dest)
    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copytree(src, dest, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns(
        "graph.db*", "__pycache__", ".demo-run", "*.pyc"))
    live = sqlite3.connect(f"{(src / '.notbydefault' / 'graph.db').resolve().as_uri()}?mode=ro",
                           uri=True)
    copy = sqlite3.connect(dest / ".notbydefault" / "graph.db")
    live.backup(copy)
    live.close()
    copy.close()
    if keep is not None:
        shutil.copytree(keep, dest / ".notbydefault" / "cache", dirs_exist_ok=True)
        shutil.rmtree(keep, ignore_errors=True)
    (dest / ".gitignore").write_text(".notbydefault/\n__pycache__/\n.claude/\n")
    git(dest, "init", "-q", "-b", "main")
    git(dest, "config", "user.email", "demo@notbydefault.local")
    git(dest, "config", "user.name", "NotByDefault demo")
    git(dest, "add", "-A")
    git(dest, "commit", "-q", "-m", "demo-app baseline (copied for the demo dataset)")
    return dest


def record_reasons(p: Path) -> list[int]:
    """Store REASONS as each decision's agent_reason (only where none is recorded)."""
    from notbydefault.graph import Graph
    done = []
    with Graph.for_project(p) as g:
        for (did, label), reason in REASONS.items():
            d = g.get_node(did)
            if not d or d["type"] != "decision" or d["label"] != label:
                print(f"  #{did} {label}: skipped (not that decision in this graph)")
                continue
            if d["data"].get("agent_reason"):
                print(f"  #{did} {label}: skipped (already has a reason)")
                continue
            g.update_data(did, agent_reason=reason, agent_reason_source=REASON_SOURCE)
            print(f"  #{did} {label}: \"{reason}\"")
            done.append(did)
    return done


def resolve(p: Path, did: int, client, apply: bool) -> None:
    from notbydefault.fit.tracing import make_tracer
    from notbydefault.resolve import Resolver, ResolveOptions
    client.step = f"resolve {did}{' --apply' if apply else ''}"
    lines: list[str] = []
    r = Resolver(p, did, ResolveOptions(apply=apply, yes=apply),
                 tracer=make_tracer(f"demo-resolve-{did}"),
                 ask=lambda q: "y", out=lines.append, client=client)
    code = r.run()
    print("\n".join(lines) + f"\n(exit {code})")
    if r.tracer.trace_id:
        traces.append((client.step, r.tracer.trace_id))
        print(f"[trace] {client.step}: {r.tracer.trace_id}")


def verifier_lift(p: Path, decision: dict | None) -> str:
    """What the verifier adds, from the decision's own results file: the recommended setup when
    it relies on the verifier, else the model the verifier lifts most. "" when nothing to cite."""
    rel = (decision or {}).get("data", {}).get("results")
    if not rel or not (p / rel).is_file():
        return ""
    res = json.loads((p / rel).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    st = {(s["model"], s["setup"]): s for s in res["stats"].values() if s.get("n_ref")}

    def correct(s):
        return round(s["correct_rate"] * s["n_ref"])
    lifts = {m: correct(st[(m, "verified")]) - correct(st[(m, "alone")])
             for m, setup in st if setup == "alone" and (m, "verified") in st}
    model, setup = res["verdict"]["recommended"]
    if setup != "verified":
        model = max(lifts, key=lifts.get, default=None)
    if model not in lifts or lifts[model] <= 0:
        return ""
    a, v = st[(model, "alone")], st[(model, "verified")]
    return (f"{model.split(':', 1)[-1]} from {correct(a)}/{a['n_ref']} to {correct(v)}/{v['n_ref']} "
            f"correct (trace {(res.get('trace_id') or '-')[:8]})")


def pivot(p: Path, client) -> None:
    """The real Pivot Check on PIVOT_PROMPT; one seeded pivot when it records nothing."""
    from notbydefault.fit.tracing import make_tracer
    from notbydefault.graph import Graph
    from notbydefault.hooks.user_prompt import handle
    from notbydefault.llm import LLMError
    from notbydefault.pivot import record
    client.step = "pivot"
    print(f'user types: "{PIVOT_PROMPT}"')
    tracer = make_tracer("demo-pivot")
    try:
        with tracer.root("notbydefault.pivot_check", {"notbydefault.prompt": PIVOT_PROMPT}):
            out, info = handle({"session_id": "demo-pivot", "hook_event_name": "UserPromptSubmit",
                                "prompt": PIVOT_PROMPT}, p, client=client, tracer=tracer)
    except LLMError as e:
        out, info = None, {"stage": f"confirm call failed ({e})"}
    tracer.flush()
    if tracer.trace_id:
        traces.append(("pivot check", tracer.trace_id))
        print(f"[trace] pivot check: {tracer.trace_id}")
    if out:
        print(out["hookSpecificOutput"]["additionalContext"])
        return
    print(f"real Pivot Check recorded nothing (stage: {info.get('stage')}); writing the seeded "
          "pivot, marked source=seeded")
    with Graph.for_project(p) as g:
        verifiers = next((n for n in g.nodes("evidence")
                          if n["label"] == "Verifiers for decision #21"), None)
        lift = verifier_lift(p, g.get_node(21))
        conflicts = [{"id": verifiers["id"], "type": "evidence", "label": verifiers["label"],
                      "why": f"the fit check measured the verifier lifting {lift}"}
                     ] if verifiers and lift else []
        imp = {"change": SEEDED_PIVOT["change"], "conflicts": conflicts,
               "decisions": [{"id": 21}]}
        pid = record(g, PIVOT_PROMPT, imp, "demo-pivot", {"model": None})
        g.update_data(pid, source=SEEDED_PIVOT["source"], source_note=SEEDED_PIVOT["source_note"])
    print(f"pivot #{pid}: {PIVOT_PROMPT} -> affects #21 (its verifiers)")


def agent_turn(p: Path) -> int | None:
    """The PreToolUse hook catches a new model choice; the reason comes from the scripted
    transcript, so the claim check has the agent's words to check."""
    from notbydefault.graph import Graph
    from notbydefault.hooks.pre_tool import handle
    print("Write digest.py (scripted transcript) -> PreToolUse hook")
    event = {"session_id": "demo-digest", "hook_event_name": "PreToolUse",
             "tool_name": "Write", "tool_use_id": "toolu_demo_digest",
             "transcript_path": str(TRANSCRIPT),
             "tool_input": {"file_path": str(p / "digest.py"), "content": DIGEST}}
    old = os.environ.get("NOTBYDEFAULT_ENTIRE")
    os.environ["NOTBYDEFAULT_ENTIRE"] = "0"       # no detached cache refresh racing the build
    try:
        out = handle(event, p)
    finally:
        if old is None:
            os.environ.pop("NOTBYDEFAULT_ENTIRE", None)
        else:
            os.environ["NOTBYDEFAULT_ENTIRE"] = old
    print(out["hookSpecificOutput"]["permissionDecisionReason"] if out else "(hook stayed silent)")
    (p / "digest.py").write_text(DIGEST, encoding="utf-8")     # the tool call runs after the hook
    with Graph.for_project(p) as g:
        hit = [d for d in g.nodes("decision") if d["session_id"] == "demo-digest"]
    if hit:
        print(f"agent's recorded reason ({hit[-1]['data'].get('agent_reason_source')}): "
              f"{hit[-1]['data'].get('agent_reason')}")
    return hit[-1]["id"] if hit else None


def screenshots(p: Path, decision: int, claims_decision: int | None) -> int:
    cmd = [sys.executable, str(REPO / "scripts" / "ui_screenshots.py"), "--project", str(p),
           "--decision", str(decision)]
    if claims_decision:
        cmd += ["--claims-decision", str(claims_decision)]
    return subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=REPO).returncode


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=str(REPO / ".demo-dataset" / "demo-app"),
                    help="the copy to (re)build (default .demo-dataset/demo-app)")
    ap.add_argument("--decision", type=int, default=21, help="decision to resolve (default 21)")
    ap.add_argument("--offline", action="store_true",
                    help="no provider calls: answer from the response cache or fall back")
    ap.add_argument("--fresh", action="store_true",
                    help="don't reuse the previous build's model-response cache")
    ap.add_argument("--no-shots", action="store_true", help="don't regenerate docs/screenshots")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    for stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
        stream.reconfigure(errors="replace", line_buffering=True)
    from notbydefault.claims import run as claims_run
    from notbydefault.env import load_env
    from notbydefault.scan import scan
    from notbydefault.stale import require
    from notbydefault.watch import watch
    load_env()

    p = copy_demo(Path(args.out).resolve(), args.fresh)
    say(f"copy ready: {p} (git repo on main)")
    client = providers(p, args.offline)
    with Step(p, "0. watch (baseline)"):
        captured("watch (baseline)", watch, p)
    with Step(p, "1. agent reasons (scripted, labelled as such)"):
        reasoned = record_reasons(p)
    with Step(p, f"2a. resolve {args.decision} (dry run)"):
        resolve(p, args.decision, client, apply=False)
    with Step(p, f"2b. resolve {args.decision} --apply (on the copy's branch; commit answered yes)"):
        resolve(p, args.decision, client, apply=True)
    with Step(p, "3. pivot"):
        pivot(p, client)
    with Step(p, "3b. agent turn: digest.py"):
        new_id = agent_turn(p)
    first = [args.decision] if args.decision in reasoned else []
    for did in first + [d for d in reasoned if d != args.decision] + [new_id] * bool(new_id):
        with Step(p, f"4. claims {did}"):
            client.step = f"claims {did}"
            captured(f"claims {did}", claims_run, p, did, client=client)
    with Step(p, f'5. require "{REQUIREMENT}"'):
        client.step = "require"
        captured("require", require, p, REQUIREMENT, client=client)
    with Step(p, "6. watch"):
        captured("watch", watch, p)
    with Step(p, "7. scan"):
        captured("scan", scan, p)
    shots = 0
    if not args.no_shots:
        with Step(p, "8. screenshots -> docs/screenshots (light + dark)"):
            shots = screenshots(p, args.decision, new_id)

    say("summary")
    print("trace ids created:")
    for step, t in traces:
        print(f"  {step:<28} {t}")
    if not traces:
        print("  none (telemetry off)")
    print(f"files written: {len(dict.fromkeys(written))}")
    print(f"provider calls made: {client.requests_made}, answered from cache: {client.cache_hits}")
    print(f"\nDataset: {p}\nUI:      python -m notbydefault ui --project \"{p}\"")
    if shots:
        print(f"screenshots failed (exit {shots})")
    return shots


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

    """The real Pivot Check on PIVOT_PROMPT; one seeded pivot when it records nothing."""
    from notbydefault.fit.tracing import make_tracer
    from notbydefault.graph import Graph
    from notbydefault.hooks.user_prompt import handle
    from notbydefault.llm import LLMError
    from notbydefault.pivot import record
    client.step = "pivot"
    print(f'user types: "{PIVOT_PROMPT}"')
    tracer = make_tracer("demo-pivot")
    try:
        with tracer.root("notbydefault.pivot_check", {"notbydefault.prompt": PIVOT_PROMPT}):
            out, info = handle({"session_id": "demo-pivot", "hook_event_name": "UserPromptSubmit",
                                "prompt": PIVOT_PROMPT}, p, client=client, tracer=tracer)
    except LLMError as e:
        out, info = None, {"stage": f"confirm call failed ({e})"}
    tracer.flush()
    if tracer.trace_id:
        traces.append(("pivot check", tracer.trace_id))
        print(f"[trace] pivot check: {tracer.trace_id}")
    if out:
        print(out["hookSpecificOutput"]["additionalContext"])
        return
    print(f"real Pivot Check recorded nothing (stage: {info.get('stage')}); writing the seeded "
          "pivot, marked source=seeded")
    with Graph.for_project(p) as g:

                          if n["label"] == "Verifiers for decision #21"), None)
        lift = verifier_lift(p, g.get_node(21))
        conflicts = [{"id": verifiers["id"], "type": "evidence", "label": verifiers["label"],
                      "why": f"the fit check measured the verifier lifting {lift}"}
                     ] if verifiers and lift else []
        imp = {"change": SEEDED_PIVOT["change"], "conflicts": conflicts,
               "decisions": [{"id": 21}]}

def agent_turn(p: Path) -> int | None:
    """The PreToolUse hook catches a new model choice; the reason comes from the scripted
    transcript, so the claim check has the agent's words to check."""
    from notbydefault.graph import Graph
    from notbydefault.hooks.pre_tool import handle
    print("Write digest.py (scripted transcript) -> PreToolUse hook")
    event = {"session_id": "demo-digest", "hook_event_name": "PreToolUse",
             "tool_name": "Write", "tool_use_id": "toolu_demo_digest",
             "transcript_path": str(TRANSCRIPT),
             "tool_input": {"file_path": str(p / "digest.py"), "content": DIGEST}}
    old = os.environ.get("NOTBYDEFAULT_ENTIRE")
    os.environ["NOTBYDEFAULT_ENTIRE"] = "0"       # no detached cache refresh racing the build
    try:
        out = handle(event, p)
    finally:
        if old is None:
            os.environ.pop("NOTBYDEFAULT_ENTIRE", None)
        else:
            os.environ["NOTBYDEFAULT_ENTIRE"] = old
    print(out["hookSpecificOutput"]["permissionDecisionReason"] if out else "(hook stayed silent)")
    (p / "digest.py").write_text(DIGEST, encoding="utf-8")     # the tool call runs after the hook
    with Graph.for_project(p) as g:
        hit = [d for d in g.nodes("decision") if d["session_id"] == "demo-digest"]
    if hit:
        print(f"agent's recorded reason ({hit[-1]['data'].get('agent_reason_source')}): "
              f"{hit[-1]['data'].get('agent_reason')}")
    return hit[-1]["id"] if hit else None


def screenshots(p: Path, decision: int, claims_decision: int | None) -> int:
    cmd = [sys.executable, str(REPO / "scripts" / "ui_screenshots.py"), "--project", str(p),
           "--decision", str(decision)]
    if claims_decision:
        cmd += ["--claims-decision", str(claims_decision)]
    return subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=REPO).returncode

    ap.add_argument("--out", default=str(REPO / ".demo-dataset" / "demo-app"),

    ap.add_argument("--decision", type=int, default=21, help="decision to resolve (default 21)")

    ap.add_argument("--fresh", action="store_true",
                    help="don't reuse the previous build's model-response cache")

    args = ap.parse_args()
    for stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
        stream.reconfigure(errors="replace", line_buffering=True)

        resolve(p, args.decision, client, apply=True)

    first = [args.decision] if args.decision in reasoned else []
    for did in first + [d for d in reasoned if d != args.decision] + [new_id] * bool(new_id):
        with Step(p, f"4. claims {did}"):
            client.step = f"claims {did}"

        client.step = "require"

    with Step(p, "6. watch"):
        captured("watch", watch, p)
    with Step(p, "7. scan"):
        captured("scan", scan, p)
    shots = 0
    if not args.no_shots:
        with Step(p, "8. screenshots -> docs/screenshots (light + dark)"):
            shots = screenshots(p, args.decision, new_id)

    print("trace ids created:")

    print(f"files written: {len(dict.fromkeys(written))}")

    if shots:

"""One live fit check of demo-app decision #21, for the record. Run by hand, never in CI.

    python scripts/live_demo_run.py                         # new live cache, every request live
    python scripts/live_demo_run.py --cache cache-live-...  # resume in that live cache
    python scripts/live_demo_run.py --no-use-fresh-cache    # reuse .notbydefault/cache like `check`

Runs `check 21` on the real demo-app with the real Groq and Gemini keys from .env. By default the
response cache is a new empty folder, .notbydefault/cache-live-<timestamp>/, so every request goes
to the providers; the old cache is left as it is. When a provider's free-tier daily quota stops
the check, the folder keeps every response so far and the script prints when the quota resets and
the command that resumes there (no request is made twice). Each attempt's trace id is kept in
<cache>/live-run.json.

The cap is --max-cost 0.10. If the check's own estimate is above that, it is raised once to 0.15
(the check refuses before any request, so that first attempt costs nothing); above 0.15 it doesn't run.

When the check finishes, the full report goes to the terminal and demo-live-run.txt, the trace id
and cost to docs/demo.md ("live-run trace: <id> ($<cost>)"), and two lines to the decision record:
"Live-run cost: ..." and "Live run: X requests on Y models across Z calendar days ...". Like any
`check`, it also updates demo-app's graph, results, failure bank and decision record.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import sys
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))

PROJECT = REPO / "demo-app"
DECISION = 21
MAX_COST = 0.10
RAISED_MAX_COST = 0.15
DAILY_LIMIT = 4                  # check's exit code when a free-tier daily quota stops it
REPORT = REPO / "demo-live-run.txt"
DEMO_DOC = REPO / "docs" / "demo.md"
STATE = "live-run.json"          # in the cache folder; the cache itself only reads */*.json
KEYS = ("GROQ_API_KEY", "GEMINI_API_KEY", "NEATLOGS_API_KEY")   # neatlogs: for the trace id
LINE = re.compile(r"^live-run trace: .*$", re.M)
ESTIMATE = re.compile(r"estimated cost: \$([0-9.]+)")
LIVE_PREFIX = "cache-live-"


# --- Pacific time without tzdata (not installed on Windows) ---------------------------------

def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--use-fresh-cache", action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction, default=True,
                    help="answer nothing from the old response cache (default: on)")
    ap.add_argument("--cache", metavar="DIR",
                    help="resume in this live cache (a folder name under demo-app/.notbydefault/, "
                         "or a path) instead of starting a new one")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    from notbydefault.env import load_env
    from notbydefault.fit.providers import ProviderSet, load_catalog
    from notbydefault.fit.run import CheckOptions, cache_dir, check_model_decision
    from notbydefault.fit.tracing import make_tracer
    from notbydefault.graph import Graph

    load_env()
    missing = [k for k in KEYS if not os.environ.get(k)]
    if missing or os.environ.get("NOTBYDEFAULT_TELEMETRY") == "0":
        print("Not running: " + (f"set {', '.join(missing)} in {REPO / '.env'}" if missing
                                 else "NOTBYDEFAULT_TELEMETRY=0 turns off the trace"))
        return 1

    if args.cache:
        cache = Path(args.cache)
        if not cache.is_absolute() and not cache.is_dir():
            cache = PROJECT / ".notbydefault" / args.cache
        if not cache.is_dir():
            print(f"Not running: no cache folder {cache}")
            return 1
        cache = cache.resolve()
    elif args.use_fresh_cache:
        cache = PROJECT / ".notbydefault" / \
            f"{LIVE_PREFIX}{datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ')}"
        cache.mkdir(parents=True)
    else:
        cache = cache_dir(PROJECT)
    live = cache.name.startswith(LIVE_PREFIX)
    attempts = load_attempts(cache) if live else []

    lines: list[str] = []

    def out(text: str = "") -> None:
        print(text, flush=True)
        lines.append(str(text))

    out(f"response cache: {cache.relative_to(REPO)} " + (
        f"(resuming: {len(cache_entries(cache))} live responses so far, {len(attempts)} earlier "
        "attempt(s); only the rest go to the providers)" if args.cache and live else
        "(new and empty: every request goes to the providers)" if live else
        "(reused: cached requests cost nothing)"))
    client = ProviderSet(load_catalog(PROJECT), cache_dir=cache)

    with Graph.for_project(PROJECT) as g:
        session = (g.get_node(DECISION) or {}).get("session_id")
    tracer = make_tracer(session)
    max_cost = MAX_COST
    from notbydefault.awake import keep_awake
    with keep_awake():
        code = check_model_decision(PROJECT, DECISION, CheckOptions(max_cost=max_cost, yes=True),
                                    client=client, tracer=tracer, out=out)
        est = next((float(m.group(1)) for l in lines if (m := ESTIMATE.search(l))), None)
        if code == 2 and est is not None and est > MAX_COST:
            max_cost = RAISED_MAX_COST
            out(f"\nEstimate ${est:.2f} is above ${MAX_COST:.2f}: raising the cap to "
                f"${max_cost:.2f} and running (nothing was spent on the refused attempt).\n")
            code = check_model_decision(PROJECT, DECISION,
                                        CheckOptions(max_cost=max_cost, yes=True),
                                        client=client, tracer=tracer, out=out)
    trace_id = tracer.trace_id
    if live and trace_id:
        attempts.append({"trace_id": trace_id, "exit": code,
                         "at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")})
        save_attempts(cache, attempts)

    with Graph.for_project(PROJECT) as g:
        decision = g.get_node(DECISION)
    results_rel = decision["data"].get("results")
    results = json.loads((PROJECT / results_rel).read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if results_rel else {}
    done = code == 0 and trace_id and results.get("trace_id") == trace_id
    req = (results.get("requests") or {}) if done else {}

    out("")
    out(f"exit code: {code}")
    out(f"cap:       --max-cost ${max_cost:.2f}")
    out(f"trace id:  {trace_id or ('none: the check did not run' if code else 'none (export failed; see the warnings above)')}")

    if code == DAILY_LIMIT and live:
        reset, pacific = next_pacific_midnight(datetime.now(timezone.utc))
        out("")
        out("A provider's free-tier daily quota stopped the check. Nothing is lost: "
            f"{len(cache_entries(cache))} live responses are kept in {cache.relative_to(REPO)}.")
        out(f"Quota resets: {pacific} (midnight Pacific) = "
            f"{reset.astimezone():%Y-%m-%d %H:%M} local ({reset:%H:%M} UTC).")
        out("Resume after that (no request is made twice):")
        out(f"  .venv\\Scripts\\python.exe scripts\\live_demo_run.py --cache {cache.name}")
        REPORT.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"report:    {REPORT.relative_to(REPO)}")
        return code

    if not done:
        REPORT.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"report:    {REPORT.relative_to(REPO)}")
        print(f"{DEMO_DOC.relative_to(REPO)} and the decision record not updated: the check did "
              f"not finish (exit {code})" + (f"; its partial trace is {trace_id}" if trace_id else "")
              + ".")
        return code or 1

    spent = record_live_run(cache if live else None, attempts, trace_id, results_rel,
                            client.pricing(), out)
    if not live:
        out(f"spent:     ${spent:.4f} ({req.get('made', 0)} provider requests, "
            f"{req.get('cache_hits', 0)} answered from the response cache)")
    out(f"results:   demo-app/{results_rel}")
    REPORT.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"report:    {REPORT.relative_to(REPO)}")
    return 0

                    pricing, out=print) -> float:

"""Build a disposable copy of demo-app for recording the demo video. See docs/recording_plan.md.

    python scripts/recording_setup.py [--out .demo-dataset/rec]

The copy is made exactly as scripts/demo_dataset.py makes one (graph.db copied read-only, git repo
on main), then:
  - the response caches of the last demo-dataset build and of #21's live run
    (demo-app/.notbydefault/cache-live-20261011T202940Z) are copied into the copy's cache, so
    `check 21` on the copy replays the live run from cache and makes no requests;
  - the scripted agent reasons are recorded (labelled as scripted, same as demo_dataset.py);
  - the NotByDefault hooks are reinstalled pointing at the copy (copied settings point at the
    real demo-app).
Nothing in demo-app/, .demo-dataset/demo-app/ or docs/ is written.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "scripts"))

from demo_dataset import copy_demo, record_reasons  # noqa: E402

CACHES = [REPO / ".demo-dataset" / "demo-app" / ".notbydefault" / "cache",
          REPO / "demo-app" / ".notbydefault" / "cache-live-20261011T202940Z"]


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=str(REPO / ".demo-dataset" / "rec"))
    out = Path(ap.parse_args().out).resolve()
    if out in {(REPO / "demo-app").resolve(), (REPO / ".demo-dataset" / "demo-app").resolve()}:
        raise SystemExit(f"--out must be a throwaway folder, not {out}")
    p = copy_demo(out)
    cache = p / ".notbydefault" / "cache"
    for src in CACHES:
        if src.is_dir():
            shutil.copytree(src, cache, dirs_exist_ok=True,
                            ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("live-run.json", "attempts.json"))
            print(f"cache: + {src.relative_to(REPO)}")
        else:
            print(f"cache: missing {src.relative_to(REPO)} (check 21 would need live requests)")
    record_reasons(p)
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "notbydefault", "install", str(p)], cwd=REPO, check=True)
    print(f"ready: {p}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
